report:
SEAT A (fresh context, not the author, claude-opus-5-5, high effort). This review covers the whole checker implementation, the addendum and the proposed GREEN envelope. It is one substantive vote. I saw no other current vote and no author vote. The source author's statements are treated as premises only. I used only the Read tool and executed, imported, compiled, hashed and wrote nothing. No new execution is authorised by this review.

READ ROUTE. I read MANIFEST.json, SEGMENT-INDEX.json and all 19 READ-SEGMENT files in order. None was truncated, and I checked that each segment continues exactly where the previous one ended. That covers every line of the 38 non-opaque originals: contract, API, test (566 lines), the three ledger files, CIP-0057, SOURCES, README, adoption record, the existing tool checker, SIZES, routing, 7 receipts, FIXTURE-STRUCTURE, three supplements plus their SOURCES, the RED envelope, design reviews A and B, the ROOT RED decision/result/precheck/stdout (0 B)/stderr, the original author manifest, the checker (lines 1-203), the notes (1-247), the addendum (1-169) and the GREEN envelope. I did not read the B9 body at all; I used only FIXTURE-STRUCTURE, SIZES and the test literals.

ACTUAL ROOT RED (my own judgment)
- The stderr shows 19 verbose lines: the 5 T00 tests 'ok' and 14 'FAIL'.
- All 14 tracebacks end with the exact text 'AssertionError: M-HASH-RED: independent_script_hash.py is absent; no implementation has been written'. Thirteen go through _impl (test:170) into _impl_source (test:150). test_static_purity goes directly through test:311 into test:150.
- The summary lines are 'Ran 19 tests' and 'FAILED (failures=14)', with no errors=.
- Root records: exit 1, stdout 0 B, stderr 11275 B.
- The before and after listings match: 1 input file plus 20 packet files (21 total), the same bytes/sha256 values (as root records them) and the same modes (0444 files in 0555 directories). The implementation was absent.
- The precheck records strict JSON, unique paths, 18 matching PINS and Ledger-Core-Script.hs absent. I compared ORIGINAL-AUTHOR-MANIFEST by eye: 19 entries, being the 18 PINS (sizes and sha strings identical to test:31-48) plus USER-OPUS55-ROUTING.md, and no Core-Script entry.
- I judge this RED acceptable as missing-implementation RED with T00 provenance intact. It is not a functional hash pass.

LINE-BY-LINE EFFECTS REVIEW (D1) OF independent_script_hash.py
- Imports (lines 20-21) are hashlib and json only.
- Module-level objects are seven constants (tuple, ints, frozenset, bytes), two sibling ValueError subclasses and ten functions. Nothing runs at import beyond creating these objects.
- Absent from the code: open, os, sys, environment, clock, random, network, subprocess, eval/exec/compile/__import__, getattr, dunder access, aliasing tricks, global or nonlocal writes, caches and closures.
- Attribute accesses, exhaustively: hashlib.blake2b, .hexdigest, bytes.fromhex, frozenset.issuperset, bytes.startswith, bytes.decode, json.loads, set.add, list.append. This matches NOTES §3.
- No name in BANNED_NAMES appears as an ast.Name. Both imports are in ALLOWED_IMPORTS.
- Inputs (str/bytes) are immutable and never stored. Results are new hexdigest strings in a new dict built in document order. Exception messages carry only indices and validated 56-hex hashes, never input reprs.
- Library exceptions are mapped after their handler exits, so they do not chain to UnicodeDecodeError.object or JSONDecodeError.doc. The remaining exposure is that traceback frames hold locals; this is disclosed.
- Allocation is bounded:
  - the str type and length are checked first (len > 65536) before the hex scan and fromhex;
  - raw type and length (≤ 1048576) are checked before decoding;
  - JSON nesting gives RecursionError and the CPython int-digit limit gives ValueError; both map to InputError;
  - NaN, Infinity and -Infinity are refused through parse_constant;
  - a BOM is refused, and decoding is explicit strict UTF-8, so json never auto-detects an encoding from bytes.
- I verified the NOTES §3 claims myself: 7 constants, 10 functions, and the builtins list.

ALGORITHM AND C4
- The digest is hashlib.blake2b(tag+code, digest_size=28).hexdigest(): native BLAKE2b-224 with digest length set in the parameter block, unkeyed, no salt or person, not truncated.
- Tags are b'\x02' for exactly 'v2' and b'\x03' for exactly 'v3', after a type-is-str check. They are not the encodeEnum index.
- The code is hashed exactly as given: no strip, no wrap, no envelope.
- C4 checks run in this order: type, length-first ≤ 65536 characters (equivalent to the 32768 B bound for even-length hex), even length, lowercase-hex frozenset, fromhex, header 0x58 with L ≥ 24 or 0x59 with L16 ≥ 256, then exact total header+L.
- C5: strict parse; top level dict; preamble dict; plutusVersion goes through the tag check; validators list of 1..64; then Phase 1 validates every entry (dict, unique non-empty str title, C4 code, 56 lowercase-hex hash, parameters absent or exactly []); then Phase 2 recomputes all entries and raises Mismatch only after all are computed.
- The two error classes are disjoint by construction.
- There are no fixture literals, receipts, oracle, UPLC, parameter application, VM or pairing code.

GREEN PREDICTION. I walked every case in the unchanged test against this source. All 19 tests are predicted to pass, conditional on three things:
- CPython BLAKE2b-224 over tag||bytes equals the Aiken-produced CIP and receipt literals. This is a shared-primitive premise, not independent evidence.
- Every B9 compiledCode is lowercase hex.
- B9 contains no NaN or Infinity tokens. T00 did not establish either B9 property.
If T01.3 fails: STOP, with no refit of tag, boundary, width or fixture. If T02.1 or T02.3 fails because of a B9 residual, that is an honest refusal: STOP, and do not relax the checker.

GREEN ENVELOPE
- Its argv matches the reviewed RED class exactly: timeout 10s with kill-after 2s; prlimit cpu 10, as 536870912, fsize 2097152, core 0; bwrap --unshare-all --die-with-parent --new-session; read-only /usr with the lib symlinks; /proc and /dev; read-only /input and /packet; --clearenv; four inner variables including MHASH_PACKET_DIR=/packet; python3 -I -B test -v; one attempt.
- /input holds exactly 2 files at 0444 in a 0555 directory: the test (a1c00918…) and the checker (9070 B, 4f6af890…). /packet holds the same 20 files, including the original MANIFEST (2f91b6fc…).
- Under -I (which includes -P), /input is not on sys.path, and the two-file listing leaves nothing to shadow stdlib modules. With no __pycache__, a read-only bind and -B, nothing can substitute for the guarded text (this closes A-F5).
- Expected result: exit 0, empty stdout, stderr with the 19 'ok' reports plus the standard separator, 'Ran 19 tests' and 'OK', and the 22 pins, modes and exact listings unchanged.
- Root must record the exact before and after entry listings (2 regular files, no symlinks, no __pycache__), as it did for RED (F3).

ADDENDUM
- D1: I agree with option (b), and I performed the line-by-line review above.
- D2, D3, D4: I agree. They are fail-closed and confined to the code paths they describe, and they cannot cause a false acceptance.
- D5, D6: accurate, with label nits (F4).
- D7: the missing tests stay source-only and are not waived. They are not needed for this single GREEN, which claims only the 19 frozen behaviours. They are required in a separately reviewed test revision before anyone relies on or adopts D2-D4 behaviours.
- D8: I agree to leave it open. That is not a closure.

My recommendation applies only to the exact one GREEN. It needs a second fresh agreeing vote (same provider, so this is context independence, not provider diversity) and a root decision. MC1-MC15 need their own separately reviewed envelope and root decision. M-HASH remains OPEN, as do all 20 UTxO families, general financial/ACTUS/DeFi, PCD/recursion, private handoff, multi-parent composition and real Preprod. Native authority is 0.

clauseAssessment.reason: impl:29 and 88 use hashlib.blake2b(..., digest_size=28).hexdigest(): native BLAKE2b-224, unkeyed, not truncated 256, rendered as 56 lowercase hex. This matches Hashes:181-182, Keys:132, B2b:57-59 and 148-162, and CIP:102. The re-export, libsodium-native-224 and CPython-equivalence links remain correctly [I].

impl:42-50 do an exact type-is-str check, then 'v2' maps to 0x02 (Lang:545) and 'v3' to 0x03 (Lang:565). Everything else, including v1/v4, case and whitespace variants and non-str values, raises InputError. The encodeEnum index (Lang:273-278, 329-330) is never used. The input is tag + code as given (Lang:205).

_digest hashes the admitted bytes as given: no strip, no extra wrap, no [enum, bytes] envelope. The payload is never decoded. Byte identity is a ledger [S] (Lang:185, 205, 261-262, 546-547, 566-567). The CBOR-Flat characterisation is [S-at-HEAD] plus [I] (D5). The vector remains a cross-check under the no-refit stop rule.

impl:64-83 check type, then length first (≤ 65536 characters, exactly the 32768 B bound for even-length hex), then even length, lowercase ASCII via a frozenset, fromhex, header 58 with L ≥ 24 or 59 with L16 ≥ 256, and exact header+L. I traced every T01.6/T01.7/T01.8/T01.9 case, including exactly 32768 B accepted and 32769 B and 1e6 characters refused. These are local tool refusals, never a different hash.

The parse is bytes-only, ≤ 1 MiB, rejects a BOM, decodes strict UTF-8, rejects duplicate keys at any depth and rejects NaN. The checks are: dict top level and preamble; required plutusVersion through the tag check; 1..64 validators; unique non-empty str titles; C4 code; 56 lowercase-hex hash; parameters absent or []. Every entry is recomputed with no group shortcut. The two error classes are disjoint. The function returns a fresh {title: hash}. All 32 T02.4 cases give InputError, and every T02.3 case gives Mismatch only.

The implementation contains no fixture, receipt or CIP literal, no oracle and no hard-coded outcome. Expected values live only in the frozen test. The receipts are same-run Aiken comparison values. The shared-primitive limitation and the absence of a ledger vector are restated in NOTES and D6.

The implementation imports only hashlib and json. My line-by-line review found no I/O, environment, clock, random, network, subprocess, dynamic execution, dunder access, aliasing, mutable module state or retained input. The AST guard is lint only. Containment is the GREEN envelope with an exact two-file read-only input and no __pycache__ (D1).

NOTES §7 and the addendum keep all the non-claims: no UPLC/flat behaviour, parameter semantics, proofs, deployability, ExUnits, ledger acceptance or dependency correspondence. All 20 families, ACTUS/DeFi/financial obligations, PCD, private handoff, multi-parent composition and Preprod remain open, and native authority is 0. Results are predictions, the author does not vote, and adoption remains a separate decision.

addendumAssessment.reason: Option (b) is correct: the guard and MC14 are lint only (attribute chains and getattr bypass them). The test is not revised and RED is not retried. I performed the mandatory line-by-line effects review: hashlib and json only, the exhaustive attribute list verified, no effects, fresh results, bounded allocation. The exact two-file read-only 0444 input in a 0555 directory, with no __pycache__ and before/after pins, closes the TOCTOU/pyc gap (A-F5). The envelope is the containment. The listing must be root-recorded (F3). Uninspected stdlib dependencies are disclosed in F6.

impl:169-203 validate the document and every entry (Phase 1) before any comparison. Phase 2 recomputes all entries and then raises Mismatch, naming the first index and the count. Any malformation therefore raises InputError regardless of entry order. This is consistent with C5 ('every entry recomputed', disjoint classes) and is fail-closed. It is untested by the frozen test, so it stays source-only (D7/F5).

impl:117-140 decode raw explicitly with strict UTF-8, so json never auto-detects UTF-16/32 from bytes. A UTF-8 BOM is refused rather than stripped. NaN/Infinity/-Infinity are refused through parse_constant. JSONDecodeError, int-limit ValueError and RecursionError map to InputError, with no chaining to exception objects that hold the input. This is a faithful reading of C5's 'strict UTF-8 JSON'. Non-finite values from finite literals in unread fields are honestly left as is.

Exact type-is checks for str/bytes/dict/list (impl:44, 64, 117, 157, 160, 164, 174, 177, 184, 186) refuse bytearray, memoryview, subclasses and bool where a str is required. This is consistent with the C4/C5 types and the T01.8 bytearray case, and is fail-closed. json with this hook yields plain dict/list/str, so valid documents are unaffected.

I verified the label corrections. Lang:117 is the PlutusLedgerLanguage import; Lang:118 is ScriptDecodeError(..); Lang:158 is P.CBORDeserialiseError; Lang:163 is P.RemainderError. Byte identity is a ledger [S], and the CBOR-Flat decode through PV2/PV3 equal to Common, plus d6eec237's dependency on 3de6f245, is [S-at-HEAD] plus [I]. All C4 refusals are local. Two nits: add Lang:185 (Plutus newtype-derived SafeToHash), and reword 'ledger accepts V1/V2 trailing bytes' as a plutus-HEAD fact plus [I] (F4).

Accurate. MC10's first-handler variant depends on order: B9's vs4 order is unverified, and FIXTURE is a root projection. The 'returns declared hash' variant is killed regardless. The positive oracle is Aiken-only with same-run receipts. The CPython/Aiken primitive is shared. The HEAD-versus-dependency, Aiken and installed-binary gaps remain, and the list of uninspected symbols matches API:86-95.

The gaps in the frozen test for the D2-D4 behaviours, fresh result, parameters:null, NaN and nesting are stated honestly. They remain source-inspected only and are not waived. My judgment is that they are not needed NOW for the single GREEN, which claims only the 19 frozen behaviours, and that these behaviours only add fail-closed refusals. A separately reviewed test revision (ADDENDUM:139-147) is required before relying on or adopting them, and readiness for anything beyond this GREEN stays blocked on that (F5).

I agree to leave it open, not closed. Titles use exact code-point equality, with lone surrogates accepted and no normalisation or added limit. Unknown fields are neither required nor validated. No CIP-57 schema closure is invented. Any future limit is a new semantic requirement needing two votes. The source matches: no unknown-field checks, and messages are index-based.
